instruction: In the open spreadsheet, enter a SUM formula in cell I33 to calculate the total of all values in the Value column (I2:I32).

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(1); pyautogui.press('enter');

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to convert xlsx to html and view in Chrome. Successfully used File > Save As to change format to HTML, saved the file, switched to Chrome, and navigated to the HTML file URL. However, the agent replaced an existing tab instead of opening a new one, causing the tab URL check to fail.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Calc menus (File > Save As), interact with dialogs (format dropdown, save button), switch to Chrome, type URLs in address bar
metadata.failure_analysis: Model replaced an existing Chrome tab when navigating to the HTML file instead of opening a new tab. The evaluator required all 4 URLs (3 original + 1 HTML file) to be present as separate tabs.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a single-app spreadsheet task (cell formula entry) within the model's demonstrated capability of interacting with LibreOffice Calc UI elements
metadata.explanation: Task requires entering a SUM formula in cell I33. Getter reads cell I33 value from the xlsx file after postconfig saves. Metric checks if value equals expected sum of 13571949 with 1% tolerance.

scoring_breakdown.formula_value: 1.0 - Cell I33 contains the correct sum (13571949)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads cell I33 from the xlsx file using data_only=True to get computed formula result
Metric correctly handles expected parameter (direct access to rules dict via expected.get('expected_value')) per get_rule behavior
Data flow is sound: getter returns {'value': <num>}, metric reads result.get('value') and compares numerically with tolerance
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S + Enter for format confirmation) before getter reads it
Numeric tolerance of 1% is reasonable for a SUM verification

Minor: evaluator checks resulting value only, not whether a SUM formula was specifically used (a hardcoded value would also pass). This is a common acceptable pattern but technically incomplete coverage of the instruction requirement.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a secondary check that reads the formula string (without data_only=True) to verify a SUM formula was used rather than a hardcoded value
